Lowry played twenty seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). A six-time [[NBA All-Star|All-Star]], he was named to the [[All-NBA Third Team]] in 2016 and won an [[NBA championship]] with the [[Toronto Raptors]] in [[2019 NBA Finals|2019]], their first and only title in franchise history. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest Raptors players of all time due to his work with turning the franchise around, from the post-[[Chris Bosh]] era to their first-ever championship in 2019. As starting point guard, Lowry played an integral role in the Raptors' success from 2012 to 2021.{{cite web|title=Why Kyle Lowry Is the Greatest Toronto Raptor of All Time|url=https://www.complex.com/sports/2020/06/why-kyle-lowry-is-the-greatest-toronto-raptor-of-all-time/|website=Complex.com|access-date=December 25, 2021}}{{cite web|title=Kyle Lowry: Appreciating the nine-year impact of the Greatest Raptor of All Time|url=https://ca.nba.com/news/kyle-lowry-appreciating-the-nine-year-impact-of-the-greatest-toronto-raptor-of-all-time/1dq7ue3j0w2e81wpdddkrbx9ag|website=NBA.com|date=August 5, 2021|access-date=December 25, 2021}}{{cite web|title=Masai Ujiri sees Kyle Lowry as 'the greatest Raptor of all time'|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/masai-ujiri-sees-kyle-lowry-greatest-raptor-time/|website=Sportsnet.ca|access-date=December 25, 2021}} Lowry was also a member of the [[United States men's national basketball team|U.S. national team]] that won a gold medal in the [[2016 Summer Olympics]]. Lowry played two seasons of [[college basketball]] with the [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcats]] before he was selected by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in the first round of the [[2006 NBA draft]] with the 24th overall pick. He appeared in three seasons with the Grizzlies before being traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in February 2009. After spending four seasons in Houston, he was traded to Toronto during the 2012 off-season, forming a backcourt duo with [[DeMar DeRozan]]. In his second season with the Raptors, he helped them reach the [[2014 NBA playoffs|playoffs]] for the first time in six years and win an [[Atlantic Division (NBA)|Atlantic Division]] title during the [[2013–14 NBA season|2013–14 season]].{{cite web|title=Kyle Lowry ready to lead Raptors to greater heights|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200921080127/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/basketball/kyle-lowry-ready-to-lead-raptors-to-greater-heights/article20902242/|work=[[The Globe and Mail]]|date=October 2, 2014|access-date=October 2, 2014|archive-date=September 21, 2020|url-status=live|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/basketball/kyle-lowry-ready-to-lead-raptors-to-greater-heights/article20902242/}} In [[2015–16 NBA season|2015–16]], he led the Raptors to a then franchise-record of 56 wins, as well as helping the team make the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] finals for the first time. In 2021, Lowry was traded to the [[Miami Heat]], where he helped the team reach the [[2023 NBA Finals]]. He later played for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] from 2024 until 2026, when he signed a one-day contract to retire with the Raptors. ==Early life== Born and raised in [[North Philadelphia]],{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/olympics/2016/player/Kyle-Terrell-Lowry|title=Kyle Terrell Lowry|publisher=FIBA|access-date=June 10, 2019}} Lowry is one of two sons of Marie Holloway and Lonnie Lowry Sr. alongside Lonnie Jr., his older brother by 5 years. His father lived 10 minutes away from the family's home,{{cite web|url=https://grantland.com/features/kyle-lowry-nba-toronto-raptors-villanova-wildcats-houston-rockets-memphis-grizzlies-demar-derozan-rudy-gay/ |title=You Can Count on Me |work=Grantland.com |date=September 23, 2014 |access-date=April 20, 2020}} which also included Lowry's cousin, Laquita. Lonnie Sr. became estranged from the family when Kyle was about seven years old, leaving him and his siblings to be raised by his mom (who worked at the [[Internal Revenue Service]] and the [[United States Postal Service|U.S. Post Office]]) as well as his disciplinarian grandmother (who worked at [[Dunkin' Donuts]]).{{cite AV media |date=April 29, 2021 |title=Kyle Lowry's Road From North Philly To Becoming An NBA Legend In Toronto - Kneading Dough Canada |medium=[[YouTube]] |language=English |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xDXuoWod-10 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/xDXuoWod-10 |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|access-date=May 3, 2021 |publisher=Uninterrupted.com}}{{cbignore}} Kyle attributes his survival and well-being to Lonnie Jr. for ensuring that he did not follow in the same path as his childhood friends who are no longer alive, including not allowing Kyle to have any tattoos and piercings. His brother was also instrumental in teaching him how to play basketball, playing pickup basketball together against older boys, and learning not to dwell on his estranged father. His brother also searched newspaper ads for [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball tryouts and ensured that Lowry would get there and make their teams.{{cite web|url=https://www.theplayerstribune.com/en-us/articles/kyle-lowry-raptors-nba-all-star |title=Growing Pains |work=ThePlayersTribune.com |date=February 11, 2016 |access-date=April 20, 2020}} ==High school career== Lowry attended [[Cardinal Dougherty High School]] in [[Philadelphia]] and played [[point guard]] for the school's varsity basketball team. Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], he was listed as the No. 6 point guard and the No. 28 player in the U.S. in 2004.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Kyle-Lowry-13709;_ylt=AtmBtjdvW8pYWUeDsYrCudhGPZB4 Kyle Lowry Recruiting Profile] ==College career== In his freshman season at [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], Lowry was named to the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Rookie team and was tabbed [[Philadelphia Big Five]] Rookie of the Year. In 24 games (3 starts), he averaged 7.5 points, 3.2 rebounds, 2.0 assists, and 1.3 steals per game.{{cite web |url=http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/lowry_kyle00.html |title=Player Bio: Kyle Lowry |access-date=January 22, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170620224148/http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/lowry_kyle00.html |archive-date=June 20, 2017 |url-status=dead}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/kyle-lowry-1.html|title=Kyle Lowry College Stats|website=Sports-reference.com|access-date=July 9, 2026}} In his [[2005–06 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|sophomore season]], he was named to the All-Big East Second Team, as well as the First Team All-Big 5. In 33 games (31 starts), he averaged 11.0 points, 4.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and 2.3 steals per game. On February 27, 2020, Lowry's jersey no. 1 was retired by the Villanova Wildcats.{{cite web |title=Kyle Lowry's jersey retired by Villanova in halftime ceremony |url=https://www.nba.com/news/kyle-lowry-villanova-jersey-retirement |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 13, 2021 |date=February 27, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Memphis Grizzlies (2006–2009)=== Lowry was selected by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] with the 24th overall pick in the [[2006 NBA draft]]. He appeared in 10 games as a rookie before suffering a broken wrist against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on November 21, 2006.{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=261121005 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170805060133/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=261121005 |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 5, 2017 |title=Gooden scores season high, Cavs fight off Grizzlies |work=ESPN.com |date=November 21, 2006 |access-date=February 6, 2019}} He subsequently underwent season-ending surgery.{{cite web|url=http://www.wmcactionnews5.com/story/5747276/grizzlies-lowry-has-wrist-surgery/ |title=Grizzlies Lowry has Wrist Surgery |website=Wmcactionnews5.com |date=November 29, 2006 |access-date=February 6, 2019}} Lowry returned for the 2007–08 season and appeared in all 82 games for the Grizzlies.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/lowryky01/gamelog/2008/ |title=Kyle Lowry 2007-08 Game Log |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=February 6, 2019}} The 2008–09 season saw Lowry and good friend [[Mike Conley Jr.]] compete for playing time and the starting point guard position. In January 2009, [[Lionel Hollins]] was named the team's head coach and Lowry was told that the team would devote the starter's minutes to Conley. Lowry was unhappy with his role, and some in the organization considered him a bad influence on the roster.[http://grantland.com/features/kyle-lowry-nba-toronto-raptors-villanova-wildcats-houston-rockets-memphis-grizzlies-demar-derozan-rudy-gay/ You Can Count on Me] ===Houston Rockets (2009–2012)=== [[File:Kyle Lowry cropped.jpg|thumb|Lowry playing for the Houston Rockets in November 2009]] On February 19, 2009, Lowry was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in a three-team deal involving the Grizzlies and the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/Rockets_Acquire_Lowry_Cook_In-301460-34.html |title=Rockets acquire Lowry, Cook in three-team deal |work=NBA.com |date=February 20, 2009 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} In Houston, Lowry grew to appreciate the tutelage of his new coach, [[Rick Adelman]]. With the Rockets making the [[NBA playoffs|playoffs]] in [[2009 NBA playoffs|2009]], Lowry played in the postseason for the first time in his career. In 2009–10, Lowry served as the backup point guard to [[Aaron Brooks (basketball)|Aaron Brooks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets_eye_brookslowry_combo_2009_09_29.html |title=Rockets Eye Brooks-Lowry Combo in the Backcourt |work=NBA.com |date=September 29, 2009 |access-date=February 6, 2019}} On December 18, 2009, he recorded a career-high 26 points, 10 assists, six rebounds, and five steals in a 116–108 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20091218/HOUDAL/gameinfo.html |title=Rockets halt Mavs' win streak behind Lowry's double-double |work=NBA.com |date=December 18, 2009 |access-date=February 6, 2019}} On June 30, 2010, with his contract expiring, the Rockets extended a qualifying offer, thus making Lowry only a [[restricted free agent]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5343492 |title=Lowry, Scola get qualifying offers |work=ESPN.com |date=June 30, 2010 |access-date=February 6, 2019}} On July 13, 2010, he signed an offer sheet with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] worth $23.5 million over four years.{{cite web|last=Feigen |first=Jonathan |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/Rockets-match-offer-sheet-to-keep-guard-Lowry-1711463.php |title=Rockets match offer sheet to keep guard Lowry |work=chron.com |date=July 14, 2010 |access-date=February 6, 2019}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/lowry_100714.html |title=Cavaliers Sign Kyle Lowry to Offer Sheet |work=NBA.com |date=July 14, 2010 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} The Rockets quickly matched the offer, thus retaining Lowry. return to relevance, the team finished the season with a 34–48 record, missing the [[NBA playoffs|playoffs]]. On May 31, 2013, [[Masai Ujiri]] was hired as the Raptors' new general manager, replacing [[Bryan Colangelo]]. Ujiri believed that Lowry had the potential to be a star, but found that his reputation around the NBA had more to do with his history of clashing with coaches and his body language than his talent. Ujiri challenged Lowry during meetings that off-season to be a better player and leader. "Do you want to be a $3 million player, $2 million player for the rest of your career", Ujiri remembers asking Lowry, "...or do you want to be a $10 million player or more?" Lowry also received mentorship from [[Chauncey Billups]], who Lowry remembers "pushed me mentally to challenge myself." Receptive to the advice he had received from Ujiri and others, Lowry looked forward to the upcoming season, entering training camp healthy for the first time in several seasons. ====2013–14 season: individual and team improvement==== The Raptors started the [[2013–14 NBA season|2013–14 season]] with a 6–12 record, until Gay, the team's leading scorer, was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]]. Following the trade, Raptors [[shooting guard]] [[DeMar DeRozan]] approached Lowry and the two decided to take ownership of the team, knowing they could both be traded if the team's management decided to rebuild rather than compete for a playoff spot. Lowry's name was linked to several teams, most frequently the [[New York Knicks]], in trade rumors, but the Knicks were reportedly unwilling to send a first-round pick to Toronto in exchange for Lowry. The post-Gay Raptors quickly emerged as one of the best teams in the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]], and many cited Lowry's strong play and leadership as a significant factor in their success.{{Cite web|url=http://www.mywebmemo.com/sports/toronto-raptors-unexpected-success-owed-in-large-part-to_152078.html|title=Toronto Raptors' unexpected success owed in large part to Kyle Lowry's magnificent season|website=Mywebmemo.com|access-date=July 9, 2026}} The team finished the season with a franchise-best 48–34 record, third in the Eastern Conference and first in the [[Atlantic Division (NBA)|Atlantic Division]] for the second time in franchise history. They made the playoffs for the first time since 2008, but lost in the first round to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] after Lowry's potential game-winning shot was blocked by [[Paul Pierce]] in game 7. Despite the disappointing end to the season, Lowry averaged a career-best 17.9 points, 7.4 assists, and 4.7 rebounds during the regular season and 21.1 points, 4.7 assists, and 4.7 rebounds during the playoffs. Lowry entered the off-season as one of the NBA's most coveted [[free agents]], attracting interest from the [[Miami Heat]], [[Houston Rockets]], and other teams.{{Cite web|url=https://torontosun.com/2014/07/02/raptors-sign-free-agent-point-guard-kyle-lowry-to-four-year-extension|title=Raptors sign free agent point guard Kyle Lowry to four-year extension|website=Torontosun.com|access-date=July 9, 2026}} On July 10, 2014, he re-signed with the Raptors to a four-year, $48 million contract.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/kylelowry_071014|title=Raptors Re-Sign Kyle Lowry | Toronto Raptors|website=Nba.com|access-date=July 9, 2026}}{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234098/Kyle-Lowry-Agrees-To-Re-Sign-With-Raptors-On-Four-Year-$48M-Deal|title=Kyle Lowry Agrees To Re-Sign With Raptors On Four-Year, $48M Deal|website=Basketball.realgm.com|access-date=July 9, 2026}} ====2014–15 season: first All-Star selection==== [[File:Kyle Lowry (17283761882).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Lowry with the Toronto Raptors in April 2015]] The Raptors and Lowry continued their strong play into the [[2014–15 NBA season|next season]], and the team once again emerged as a top [[seed (sports)|seed]] in the Eastern Conference. On November 7, 2014, Lowry became the team's all-time leader for [[Double (basketball)|triple-doubles]] with a 13-point, 10 assist, and 11 rebound performance in a win against the [[Washington Wizards]]. It was Lowry's sixth career triple-double and his fourth as a Raptor, passing [[Damon Stoudamire]], who had the previous franchise record of three.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141107/WASTOR/gameinfo.html |title=Lowry leads Raptors past Wizards 103-84 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 10, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141221065359/http://www.nba.com/games/20141107/WASTOR/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 21, 2014 |url-status=dead}} On December 3, he scored a career-high 39 points on 13-of-22 shooting in a win against the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141203/TORUTA/gameinfo.html |title=Lowry scores 39, Raptors hand Jazz 7th loss in row |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 5, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909055519/http://www.nba.com/games/20141203/TORUTA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=September 9, 2017 |url-status=dead}} On January 5, 2015, Lowry was named the Eastern Conference player of the month for December 2014, making him only the second Raptor, after [[Chris Bosh]], to receive this recognition.
